SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r1.claim: The majority read نصليهم with a damma on nūn, from the form أصلى.
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: { نصليهم }: بضم النون من أصلى

SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r2.speaker: حميد
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r2.claim: Humayd reads نصليهم with fatḥa on nūn, from the triliteral صلي.

SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r3.speaker: سلام ويعقوب
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r3.claim: Salam and Yaqub read the pronoun with a damma on hāʾ, a Hijazi dialect form.
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r3.anchor: وسلام ويعقوب: نصليهم " بضم الهاء وهي لغة الحجاز

SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r4.claim: كلما is a temporal adverb governed by بدلناهم; its clause is circumstantial from the object pronoun in نصليهم.
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r4.anchor: قد تقدم الكلام على " كلما " وأنها ظرف زمان، والعامل فيها " بدلناهم " والجملة في محل نصب على الحال

SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r5.claim: The كلما clause could describe نارا with an omitted resumptive pronoun, but the author says this analysis is weak.
SAMIN-DURR:4:56/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون صفة ل " نارا " والعائد محذوف وليس بالقوي

ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r4.claim: Nuṣlīhim nāran means We roast them in a fire.
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r4.anchor: (سوف نصليهم نارا) أي نشويهم في نار.

ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r5.claim: A report says a Jewish woman gave the Prophet a maṣliyya sheep, meaning roasted sheep, illustrating the word.
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r5.anchor: ويروى أن يهودية أهدت إلى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - شاة مصلية أي مشوية.

ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r6.claim: Zajjāj prefers pronouncing the tāʾ in naḍijat distinctly before jīm to avoid too many jīm sounds; assimilation is also allowed.
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r6.anchor: الأحسن إظهار التاء ههنا مع الجيم. لئلا تكثر الجيمات، وإن شئت أدغم التاء في الجيم

ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r7.claim: Assimilation into jīm is possible because jīm is from the middle of the tongue, tāʾ from its tip, and tāʾ is voiceless.
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r7.anchor: لأن الجيم من وسط اللسان والتاء من طرفه، والتاء حرف مهموس فأدغمته في الجيم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r8.claim: It is wrong to say sinful skin is replaced by skin that did not sin: the human, not the skin, sins and feels pain.
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r8.anchor: فإن قال قائل بدل الجلد الذى عصى بالجلد الذي غير العاصي، فذلك غلط من القول. لأن العاصي والآلم هو الإنسان لا الجلد.

ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r9.claim: The replacement may be renewed maturation, restoring the skin as before; like reshaping a ring, the silver remains one substance.
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r9.anchor: وجائز أن يكون بدل الجلد النضج. وأعيد كما كان جلده الأول، كما تقول: قد صغت من خاتمي خاتما آخر فأنت وإن غيرت الصوغ فالفضة أصل واحد.

ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r10.claim: Skin had decayed after resurrection; recreating it after maturation is like recreating it after resurrection.
ZAJJAJ:v2p64#2/r10.anchor: وقد كان الجلد بلي بعد البعت، فإنشاؤه بعد النضج كإنشائه بعد البعث.

ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r1.claim: The purpose is to make the pain of punishment reach them fully.

ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r2.claim: Al-ʿazīz achieves His will and cannot be overcome; He is also ḥakīm in the way He governs.
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r2.anchor: العزيز البالغ إرادته، الذي لا يغلبه

ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r3.claim: In answer to skeptics who might ask about punishment, God states that all He does is governed by wisdom.
ZAJJAJ:v2p65/r3.anchor: لأن الملحدين ربما سألوا عن العذاب كيف وقع فأعلم الله عز وجل أن جميع ما فعله بحكمة.

ASAD-NOTES:4:56#n73/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:4:56#n73/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:4:56#n73/r1.claim: Razi reads the replacement of burnt skins as an allegory emphasizing the long duration of afterlife suffering.
ASAD-NOTES:4:56#n73/r1.anchor: This awesome allegory of suffering in the life to come is obviously meant to bring out the long-lasting nature of that suffering (Razi).

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p191/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p191/r1.speaker: حميد بن قيس
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p191/r1.claim: Ḥumayd ibn Qays reads سوف نصليهم نارا; Ibn Jinnī says its analysis was already given earlier in the book.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p191/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك1 قراءة حميد بن قيس2: "سوف نصليهم نارا"3.

NASHR:v2p5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p5/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p5/r1.claim: For the jīm in نضجت جلودهم, some Ibn Dhakwān transmitters show the tāʾ and others assimilate it; the author finds the Shāṭibī’s reported disagreement unsupported by the cited routes.
NASHR:v2p5/r1.anchor: وروى ابن مرشد وأبو طاهر وابن عبد الرزاق، وغيرهم عن الأخفش عنه نضجت جلودهم بالإظهار، ووجبت جنوبها بالإدغام

NASHR:v2p5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p5/r4.speaker: أبو الفتح فارس
NASHR:v2p5/r4.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ’s text has assimilation from Hishām before jīm and showing from Ibn Dhakwān, without distinguishing وجبت from the other example.
NASHR:v2p5/r4.anchor: الإدغام عن هشام في الجيم والإظهار عن ابن ذكوان

NASHR:v2p5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p5/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p5/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Abū Jaʿfar, Yaʿqūb, Qālūn, and al-Aṣbahānī from Warsh show the tāʾ at the six following letters; exceptional reports give Ruways assimilation at sīn, jīm, and ẓāʾ, and Rawḥ at ẓāʾ only.
NASHR:v2p5/r6.anchor: والباقون بإظهارها عند الأحرف الستة وهم ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو جعفر ويعقوب وقالون والأصبهاني عن ورش

QIRAAT-ER:4:56:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:4:56:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:4:56:7#1/r1.claim: The pronoun suffix alternates from -him to -hum after kasra as a dialectal phonological variant, without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:4:56:7#1/r1.anchor: Pronoun vowel shift: -him to -hum; standard dialectal alternation in pronoun suffix

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r10.claim: Nudj is the start of decay and separation of parts, as with meat and fruit ripening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p665#2/r10.anchor: النضج: أخذ الشيء في التهري وتفرق أجزائه، ومنه نضج اللحم، ونضج الثمرة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r7.claim: After mentioning the divided response and Hell for those who turn away, the passage describes disbelievers' punishment and then believers' reward, paralleling another verse's contrast.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r7.anchor: لما ذكر قوله: ومنهم من صد عنه، وكفى بجهنم سعيرا أتبع ذلك بما أعد الله للكافرين بآياته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r8.speaker: حميد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r8.claim: Hamid reads the verb from ṣ-l-y rather than the majority's form from aṣlā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور نصليهم من أصلى. وقرأ حميد: نصليهم من صليت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r9.speaker: سلام ويعقوب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r9.claim: Sallam and Ya'qub read the pronoun suffix with ḍamma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r9.anchor: وقرأ سلام ويعقوب: نصليهم بضم الهاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r10.claim: “Every time” is an adverbial phrase added to temporal maṣdariyya mā and governed by “replace”; its clause carries conditional force, is circumstantial, and is governed by “make them enter.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r10.anchor: انتصاب كل على الظرف لأنه مضاف إلى ما المصدرية الظرفية، والعامل فيه بدلناهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r11.claim: Replacement can change qualities while preserving an entity or replace the entity itself; the apparent sense is a new skin after the former one softens, withers, and disappears.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r11.anchor: والتبديل على معنيين: تبديل في الصفات مع بقاء العين، وتبديل في الذوات بأن تذهب العين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r12.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says skins grow from flesh, so when a sinner's skin burns God replaces it with another skin made from that person's flesh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r12.anchor: قال السدي: إن الجلود تخلق من اللحم، فإذا أحرق جلد بدله الله من لحم الكافر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r13.claim: Another view says the same skins return after burning, as bodies are restored after decay in graves, so their qualities change but not their identity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r13.anchor: وقيل: هي بعينها تعاد بعد إحراقها، كما تعاد الأجساد بعد البلى في القبور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r14.speaker: الفضيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r14.claim: Al-Fudayl interprets the process as making what was cooked become uncooked again.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r14.anchor: وقال الفضيل: يجعل النضيج غير نضيج.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r15.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r15.claim: One view says skins are replaced seven times each day; al-Hasan says seventy times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r15.anchor: وقيل: تبدل كل يوم سبع مرات. وقال الحسن: سبعين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r16.claim: Abu Hayyan calls far-fetched the view that the skins are tar garments mixed inseparably with bodies and replaced a hundred or even a hundred thousand times daily.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r16.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أن الجلود هي سرابيل من قطران تخالط جلودهم مخالطة لا يمكن إزالتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r17.claim: He also rejects as far-fetched the metaphor that each apparent end of the torment begins anew, expressing its uninterrupted duration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r17.anchor: وأبعد أيضا من ذهب إلى أن هذا استعارة عن الدوام، كلما انتهى فقد ابتدأ من أوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r18.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people of Hell are clothed in white skins like sheets of paper.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r18.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يلبسهم الله جلودا بيضاء كأنها قراطيس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r19.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r19.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya says the people of Hell wear skins that feel pain although the skins themselves do not feel it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p679/r19.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى: يلبس أهل النار جلودا تؤلمهم ولا تؤلم هي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r1.claim: Each new skin lets them taste pain again; “taste” suggests an initial painful sensation, preventing habituation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r1.anchor: ليذوقوا العذاب أي ذلك التبديل كلما نضجت الجلود، هو ليذوقوا ألم العذاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the phrase to mean punishment continues without interruption, like praying that someone remain in honor and increase in it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ليذوقوا العذاب ليدوم لهم دونه ولا ينقطع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r3.claim: God is invincible and cannot be overcome, and wise in placing things where they belong.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r3.anchor: إن الله كان عزيزا حكيما أي عزيزا لا يغالب، حكيما يضع الأشياء مواضعها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says nothing can prevent God from doing what He wills to criminals, and that His wisdom means He punishes only those who deserve it, justly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p680/r4.anchor: الزمخشري: عزيز لا يمتنع عليه شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.claim: The verse resumes the preceding discussion as explanation: its referent is either those rejecting Muhammad or everyone rejecting any prophet, and the signs then include all prophetic proofs.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r1.anchor: استنئاف وقع كالبيان والتقرير لما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.claim: Sibawayh says sawfa signals threat and warning, with the shorter sa serving similarly, as in 74:26.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r2.anchor: كما قال سيبويه : كلمة تذكر للتهديد والوعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.claim: Sawfa and sa can also promise good, as in 93:5 and 12:98, though they often intensify a threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r3.anchor: وقد تذكر للوعد كما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r4.claim: The indefinite fire magnifies it: they will certainly enter a formidable fire.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.claim: Nadhijat means the skins are thoroughly cooked, consumed, and disintegrated, by analogy with ripened fruit or meat.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r5.anchor: من نضج الثمر واللحم نضجا ونضجا إذا أدرك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.claim: Kullama is a temporal adverb governed by baddalnahum: at each skin's burning, God gives another skin in its place.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r6.anchor: و ( كلما ) ظرف زمان والعامل فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r7.claim: The objection that the replacement skin did not sin mistakes the skin for the responsible subject: skin lacks perception and agency, like an instrument such as a killer's hand or sword.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r7.anchor: وذلك لأنه هو العاصى باعتبار أصله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r8.claim: Pain and reward belong to the sentient soul in whatever body it inhabits; bodily parts change during life, so continuity need not mean identical matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r8.anchor: فالحق أن العذاب على النفس الحساسة بأي بدن حلت وفي أي جلد كانت

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.claim: The enormous bodies described for Hell and Paradise show that people need not perform worldly deeds with precisely those bodies; an iron body example also defeats the objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r9.anchor: وأن سن الجهنمي كجبل أحد وأن أهل الجنة يدخلونها على طول آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r10.claim: If bodily resurrection were not established as necessary religious doctrine, purely spiritual reward and punishment would not be rationally implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p58#2/r10.anchor: ولولا ما علم من الدين بالضرورة من المعاد الجسماني بحيث صار إنكاره كفرا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r1.claim: Al-Alusi does not deny that annihilated bodies can be recreated; he says re-creation is unnecessary though possible, and either identity or similar-body accounts preserve bodily resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r1.anchor: ولا يتوهم من هذا إني أقول باستحالة إعادة المعدوم معاذ الله تعالى ولكني أقول بعدم الحاجة إلى إعادته

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r2.claim: Scriptural evidence differs between restoring the same bodies after annihilation and creating similar bodies while the first perish; either can be accepted with bodily resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r2.anchor: فمنها ما يدل على إعادة الأجسام بعينها بعد إعدامها ومنها ما يدل على خلق مثلها وفناء الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r3.claim: Al-Alusi says he will later discuss texts that appear to show bodily identity, including tongues, hands, and feet testifying in 24:24.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r3.anchor: مثل قوله سبحانه : ( يوم تشهد عليهم ألسنتهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم بما كانوا يعملون )

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r4.speaker: السفيري
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r4.claim: Al-Safiri's commentary reports the soul and body blaming each other, with an angel comparing them to a seeing cripple and blind man who jointly take fruit; al-Alusi rejects the analogy because the bodily instrument lacks choice and awareness.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r4.anchor: وما في شرح البخاري للسفيري من أنه لا تزال الخصومة بين الناس حتى تختصم الروح والجسد

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r5.claim: The soul-body garden parable fails because the bodily instrument has no choice or awareness; only an unknown form of consciousness could alter the comparison.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r5.anchor: لظهور الفرق بين المثال والممثل له فإن الحامل فيما نحن فيه لا اختيار له ولا شعور

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r6.claim: The skin replacement can occur many times in one hour.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r6.anchor: ثم إن هذا التبديل كيفما كان يكون في الساعة الواحدة مرات كثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r7.claim: Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nuʿaym report from Ibn ʿUmar that Kaʿb explained skins are replaced 120 times in an hour and ʿUmar affirmed hearing this from the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : قرئ عند عمر هذه الآية فقال كعب : عندي تفسيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r8.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r8.claim: Ibn Abi Shayba and others report from al-Hasan that the fire consumes a person's flesh 70,000 times daily, each time telling them to return.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r8.anchor: عن الحسن قال : بلغني أنه يحرق أحدهم في اليوم سبعين ألف مرة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r9.claim: “Taste the punishment” means experience continues without interruption; tasting also conveys bitterness, acute impact, and inward penetration.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r9.anchor: أي ليدوم ذوقه ولا ينقطع كقولك للعزيز : أعزك الله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r10.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r10.claim: A wisdom for changing skins is to prevent souls from imagining that perception ends in burning or that pain may be spared as the body is spared burning.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r11.claim: Another proposed wisdom is that renewal creates despair and grief upon grief.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r11.anchor: وقيل : السر في ذلك أن في النضج والتبديل نوع إياس لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r12.claim: Some deny literal burning and replacement of skins, claiming the replacement refers to garments in 14:50 called skins by proximity; al-Alusi rejects this as departing from the plain sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r12.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم نضج الجلود بالمعنى المتبادر وتبديلها زاعما أن التبديل إنما هو للسرابيل

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r13.claim: The garment reading is an unwarranted departure from the plain text and established teaching; literal skin replacement is within God's power.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r13.anchor: وفيه أنه ترك للظاهر ويوشك أن يكون خلاف المعلوم ضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r14.claim: ʿAziz means ever invincible, unopposed and unprevented.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r14.anchor: عزيزا أي لم يزل منيعا لا يدافع ولا يمانع

ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r15.claim: Another explanation takes ʿaziz to mean capable of carrying out whatever God threatens or promises.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p59/r15.anchor: وقيل : إنه قادر لا يمتنع عليه ما يريده مما تواعد أو وعد به

ALUSI-FULL:v5p60/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p60/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p60/r1.claim: Hakim describes God's governance, decree, and punishment; the clause explains the preceding casting into fire and skin replacement, with the divine name emphasized to ground the ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p60/r1.anchor: في تدبيره وتقديره وتعذيب من يعذبه والجملة تعليل لما قبلها من الإصلاء والتبديل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r1.claim: “We shall put them into it” means that God will enter them into the Fire; “ripened” means burned.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r2.claim: The replacement skins are different from the burned skins; Ibn ʿAbbās says they will be white, like sheets of paper.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r2.anchor: غير الجلود المحترقة، قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يبدلون جلودا بيضاء كأمثال القراطيس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r3.speaker: عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r3.claim: When asked by ʿUmar, Muʿādh explained the skins would be replaced one hundred times in an hour; ʿUmar said he had heard this from the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r3.anchor: فقال معاذ: عندي تفسيرها: تبدل في ساعة مائة مرة، فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: هكذا سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r4.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Fire consumes them seventy thousand times each day, and each time they are restored as they were.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: تأكلهم النار كل يوم سبعين ألف مرة كلما أكلتهم قيل لهم عودوا فيعودون كما كانوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r5.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the distance between a disbeliever's shoulders is a three-day journey for a swift rider.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: "ما بين منكبي الكافر مسيرة ثلاثة أيام للراكب المسرع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet said a disbeliever's molar or tusk will be like Mount Uḥud and the thickness of his skin a three-day journey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنهم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ضرس الكافر أو ناب الكافر مثل أحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r7.claim: Asked how newly made skins that did not sin can be punished, Baghawī answers that the original skin is restored each time.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r7.anchor: فإن قيل: كيف تعذب جلود لم تكن في الدنيا ولم تعصه؟ قيل يعاد الجلد الأول في كل مرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r8.claim: “Other” skins can be the same underlying skin with a changed quality, like a ring remade from the same ring; similarly one may call a changed brother someone other than the one remembered.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p237/r8.anchor: لتبدل صفتها، كما تقول: صنعت من خاتمي خاتما غيره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r1.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r1.claim: Al-Suddī says a disbeliever's skin is replaced by skin from his flesh; it becomes flesh, then another skin emerges from the flesh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r1.anchor: وقال السدي: يبدل الجلد جلدا غيره من لحم الكافر ثم يعيد الجلد لحما ثم يخرج من اللحم جلدا آخر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r2.claim: Some say the person, rather than the skin itself, experiences the punishment, citing the wording “so they may taste the punishment.”

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r3.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r3.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā says God clothes the people of Hell in skins that do not feel pain, replacing each burned skin; as with tar garments, the person suffers though the garment itself does not.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p238/r3.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى: إن الله عز وجل يلبس أهل النار جلودا لا تألم، فيكون زيادة عذاب عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r1.claim: The verse explains and confirms the preceding warning.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r2.claim: The same skin may be restored in a new form, like changing a ring into an earring, or its burned surface renewed so that it can again feel punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r2.anchor: بأن يعاد ذلك الجلد بعينه على صورة أخرى كقولك:

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r3.claim: The renewed sensation lets them continue tasting the punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r3.anchor: { ليذوقوا العذاب } أي ليدوم لهم ذوقه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r4.claim: Another view says a new skin is created; the actual recipient of punishment is the conscious sinful soul, not its sensory instrument, so there is no difficulty.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r4.anchor: وقيل يخلق لهم مكانه جلد آخر والعذاب في الحقيقة للنفس العاصية

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r5.claim: God is mighty: nothing can prevent what He wills.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:56/r6.claim: God is wise and punishes in accordance with His wisdom.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r1.claim: Disbelievers conceal what their intellects disclosed through God’s signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r1.anchor: أي ستروا ما أظهرته عقولهم بسببها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r2.claim: God’s promise to put them in the Fire is certain even if they receive a long reprieve.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r2.anchor: بوعد ثابت وإن طال معه الإمهال

BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r3.claim: When skins reach the state of cooked meat, like dead flesh in a wound, they no longer feel pain.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r3.anchor: الذي أدرك أن يؤكل , فصارت كاللحم الميت

BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r4.claim: God restores skins to their pre-burning state; like reshaping a silver ring, the material remains while its form changes, so the new skin differs in form.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r4.anchor: قبل تسليط النار عليها , كما إذا صغت من خاتم خاتما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r5.claim: Renewed skins renew the tasting of torment and the spectacle of restoration, matching their repeated denials; otherwise their worn bodies would perish and their punishment end.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r5.anchor: فتجدد لهم مشاهدة الإعادة بعد البلى كل وقت

BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r6.claim: God is unconquerable and perfects His acts; He apportions punishment to sins because the condemned intended to persist in them for as long as they lived.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p269/r6.anchor: يتقن صنعه , فجعل عذابهم على قدر ذنوبهم

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r1.claim: God's signs here mean the Qur'an and the other miracles.

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r2.claim: Sawfa can signal a threat or warning, as here, and can also signal a promise, adding emphasis.

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r3.claim: The phrase means admitting the unbelievers into a vast, dreadful fire.

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r4.claim: The skins' ripening means their being burned through.

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r5.claim: Here other skins differ in form, not underlying identity: the very same skin is remade in another form, as metal is melted and shaped into a different ring.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r5.anchor: والحاصل أنه يعاد ذلك الجلد بعينه على صورة أخرى كقولك صغت من خاتمي خاتما غيره

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r6.claim: The apparent objection is that replacing a burned, sinful skin with an unoffending one would punish the innocent; the answer is that the sensitive skin that sinned is punished, and its identity remains one.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r6.anchor: قلت : العذاب للجلدة الحساسة وهي التي عصت لا للجلد مطلقا والذات واحدة

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r7.claim: Tasting means their experience of punishment continues without interruption or diminution, like wishing someone lasting increase in honor.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r7.anchor: أي ليدوم لهم ذوقه ولا ينقطع كقولك للعزيز أعزك الله أي أدامك على عزك

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Fire consumes them seventy times each day; each time they are told to return, they return as they were.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r8.anchor: قال الحسن : تأكلهم النار في كل يوم سبعين مرة

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r9.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r9.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet describes an unbeliever's skin as forty cubits, his tooth as large as Uhud, and his upper lip reaching his navel, with running worms, camel-neck snakes, and mule-sized scorpions between flesh and skin.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r9.anchor: وروي مرفوعا أن جلد الكافر أربعون ذراعا وضرسه مثل أحد وشفته العليا تضرب سرته

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r10.claim: Such added size and creatures do not punish an innocent new body; the added weight itself burdens the sinner, like Hell's chains, fetters, snakes, and scorpions.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r10.anchor: لكن إذا زيد ذلك ثقلة على العبد ويكون نفس الثقل عقوبة عليه كسائر عقوبات جهنم

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r11.claim: Although they already suffer severely, tasting describes how each renewed exposure is felt like tasting something, without pain fading through burning or continued exposure.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r11.anchor: إحساسهم بالعذاب في كل مرة كإحساس الذائق بالمذوق من حيث أنه لا يدخله نقصان

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r12.claim: Renewing the skins makes clear that sensation persists, since people might otherwise imagine that burning destroys perception; God could preserve perception or bodies without this renewal.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r12.anchor: ولعل السر في تبديل الجلود مع قدرته تعالى على بقاء إدراك العذاب وذوقه بحاله

BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r13.claim: God is mighty, so nothing can prevent what He wills for wrongdoers, and wise in the punishment He assigns.
BURSEVI:v2p177#2/r13.anchor: لا يمتنع عليه شيء مما يريده بالمجرمين

DURR-FULL:v2p544/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p544/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p544/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's being described as mighty, wise, knowing, and powerful is not past and finished: God always was and remains so.
DURR-FULL:v2p544/r2.anchor: وأما قوله (وكان الله) فإن الله كان ولم يزل كذلك وهو كذلك (عزيز حكيم) (عليم قدير)

DURR-FULL:v2p568/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that when the skins burn, God replaces them with white skins like sheets of paper.
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر في قوله {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} قال: إذا احترقت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا بيضاء أمثال القراطيس

DURR-FULL:v2p568/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r2.speaker: معاذ
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r2.claim: Muʿādh explains that the skins are replaced one hundred times in an hour; ʿUmar confirms that he heard this from the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قرىء عند عمر {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها ليذوقوا العذاب} فقال معاذ: عندي تفسيرها تبدل في ساعة مائة مرة

DURR-FULL:v2p568/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r3.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r3.claim: Kaʿb says he read before Islam that the replacement happens 120 times in an hour; ʿUmar confirms hearing that figure from the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r3.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: تلا رجل عند عمر {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} فقال كعب عندي تفسير هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v2p568/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that a person is burned 70,000 times in a day; once the fire consumes the flesh, they are told to return and do so.
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r4.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية قال: بلغني أنه يحرق أحدهم في اليوم سبعين ألف مرة

DURR-FULL:v2p568/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the fire strips away the skin until it reaches the bones, then God replaces it; this lasts forever because of their denial of the Messenger and God's signs.
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك في الآية قال: تأخذ النار فتأكل جلودهم حتى تكشطها عن اللحم حتى تفضي النار إلى العظام

DURR-FULL:v2p568/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r6.speaker: يحيى بن يزيد الحضرمي
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r6.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī reports that a disbeliever has one hundred skins, with a different color of punishment between each pair.
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r6.anchor: عن يحيى بن يزيد الحضرمي أنه بلغه في قول الله {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها}

DURR-FULL:v2p568/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says an earlier book described each person's skin as forty cubits, teeth as seventy cubits, and belly large enough for a mountain; consumed skins are replaced.
DURR-FULL:v2p568/r7.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس في الآية قال: سمعنا أنه مكتوب في الكتاب الأول: أن جلد أحدهم أربعون ذراعا وسنه سبعون ذراعا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the word سوف expresses a threat.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قوله : سوف قال : وعيد

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r2.claim: Ibn Umar explains that the skins are burned whenever they are described as ripened.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر في قوله : كلما نضجت جلودهم قال : اذا احترقت جلودهم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r3.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r3.claim: Mu'adh ibn Jabal says the skins are replaced one hundred times in an hour; Umar confirms he heard this from the Messenger of God.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r3.anchor: فقال معاذ بن جبل : عندي تفسيرها : تبدل في ساعة مائة مرة ، فقال عمر

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r4.claim: Ibn Umar says that after the skins burn, they are replaced with white skins like sheets of paper.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر في قوله : كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلدا غيرهاقال اذا احترقت جلودهم بدلوا جلودا بيضاء امثال القراطيس

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r5.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas reports that an earlier scripture describes a person's skin as forty cubits and gives a ninety-cubit measure for his سن; his belly could hold a mountain, and consumed skins are replaced.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r5.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس قولهكلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها قال : سمعنا انه مكتوب في الكتاب الاول

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says the skins are cooked seventy thousand times each day.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r6.anchor: عن الحسن ، قوله : كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها قال : تنضجهم في اليوم سبعين الف مرة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r7.speaker: فضيل بن هشام
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r7.claim: Fudayl ibn Hisham adds, reporting from al-Hasan, that after the fire consumes the flesh, they are told to return and do so.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r7.anchor: زاد فيه فضيل بن هشام عن الحسن : كلما انضجتهم واكلت لحومهم ، قيل لهم : عودوا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r8.speaker: يحيى بن يزيد الحضرمي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r8.claim: Yahya ibn Yazid al-Hadrami reports that an unbeliever is given one hundred skins, with a different punishment color between each pair.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p982/r8.anchor: عن يحيى بن يزيد الحضرمي انه بلغه في قول الله تعالى كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها ليذوقوا العذاب قال : يجعل للكافر مائة جلد

IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains العزيز as mighty in His vengeance when He punishes; Qatada and al-Rabi ibn Anas are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية عزيزا حكيما يقول : عزيزا في نقمته اذا انتقم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq glosses العزيز as God's power to support or aid against disbelievers whenever He wills.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p983/r2.anchor: قال : قال محمد بن اسحاق : العزيز في نصرته ممن كفر اذا شاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r1.claim: This is a threat to all disbelievers, broader than the preceding passage and functioning as its coda, which explains why it is set apart.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r1.anchor: تهديد ووعيد لجميع الكافرين ، فهي أعم مما قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r2.claim: Iṣlāʾ means roasting meat over fire; Ibn Ashur links this wording to the earlier discussions at 4:10 and 4:30.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r3.claim: Naṣlīhim has a damma on its initial nūn and derives from the form ifʿāl.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r4.claim: Nadijat means reaching the final degree of cooking or roasting.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r5.claim: Replacing implies difference, so ghayrahā reinforces what badalnāhum already entails; nāran is a second object because the verb follows the pattern of aʿṭā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p89#2/r5.anchor: فقوله : { غيرها } تأكيد لما دل عليه فعل التبديل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r1.claim: The skin carries the sensation of punishment to the soul by God's customary creation; without replacing it after burning, the soul would no longer feel the fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r1.anchor: لأن الجلد هو الذي يوصل إحساس العذاب إلى النفس بحسب عادة خلق الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r2.claim: Changing the skin while keeping its owner is just because skin transmits, rather than constitutes, the punishment; resurrection preserves identity through the same soul and a body derived from the original, as a palm comes from a seed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r2.anchor: وتبديل الجلد مع بقاء نفس صاحبه لا ينافي العدل لأن الجلد وسيلة إبلاغ العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r3.claim: He invokes an unspecified report that resurrection involves regrowth from the coccygeal bone, treating what grows from something as belonging to it, like a palm from a seed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r3.anchor: إنبات من أعجاب الأذناب ، حسبما ورد به الأثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r4.claim: God's might enables complete punishment of those who defy Him, while His wisdom accounts for the particular manner of their being burned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p90/r4.anchor: فالعزة يتأتى بها تمام القدرة في عقوبة المجترىء على الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r1.claim: After describing rebellious Israelites and their sins, the passage gives an explicit warning broadly applying to them and all who commit the same unbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r1.anchor: تقدم في الآيات وصف المردة من بني إسرائيل وذكر أفعالهم وذنوبهم، ثم جاء بالوعيد النص لهم بلفظ جلي عام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r2.claim: The common reading has ḍamma on the nūn, from aṣlā, meaning to bring them near the fire and cast them into it; it is equivalent in sense to ṣallaytu with doubled lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r2.anchor: والقراءة المشهورة نصليهم بضم النون من أصليت ومعناه قربت من النار وألقيت فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r3.speaker: حميد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r3.claim: Humayd reads the initial nūn with fatḥa, from ṣalaytu, meaning “roasted”; a hadith uses maṣliyya for a roasted sheep.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r3.anchor: وقرأ حميد «نصليهم» بفتح النون من صليت، ومعناه شويت، ومنه الحديث، أتي رسول الله بشاة مصلية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r4.speaker: سلام ويعقوب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r4.claim: Salam and Yaʿqub read nuṣlīhim with a ḍamma on the hāʾ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r5.claim: One group says new skins are supplied because the souls suffer while skins themselves do not feel; replacing them renews the punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r5.anchor: فقالت فرقة: تبدل عليهم جلود غيرها، إذ نفوسهم هي المعذبة والجلود لا تألم في ذاتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r6.claim: Another group says God continually restores the very same skin from earthly life; it is called replacement because its qualities change before restoration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة: «تبديل الجلود» هو إعادة ذلك الجلد بعينه الذي كان في الدنيا، تأكله النار ويعيده الله دأبا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r7.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that whenever their skins burn, they are replaced by white skins like sheets of paper.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عمر، كلما احترقت جلودهم بدلوا جلودا بيضاء كالقراطيس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r8.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r8.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan says the skins are replaced seventy thousand times in a day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن، تبدل عليهم في اليوم سبعين ألف مرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r9.claim: A group, as al-Tabari relates, takes the “skins” to be garments of tar that cling like skin and are replaced continually.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r9.anchor: وقالت فرقة: الجلود في هذا الموضع سرابيل القطران، سماها جلودا للزومها فصارت كالجلود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r10.claim: God’s might and wisdom suit this warning: no rival can overcome Him, and He acts only with wisdom and right judgment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p69/r10.anchor: لأن الله لا يغالبه مغالب إلا غلبه الله، ولا يفعل شيئا إلا بحكمة وإصابة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains nuslihim as roasting them in a fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج أي نشويهم في نار ويروى أن يهودية أهدت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r2.claim: A report says a Jewish woman once gave the Prophet a roasted sheep; the word masliyya means roasted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r2.anchor: ويروى أن يهودية أهدت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شاة مصلية أي مشوية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r3.claim: One view takes the replacement skins literally; the skins convey punishment as they once conveyed pleasure, while the people, not the skins, are punished.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنها غيرها حقيقة ولا يلزم على هذا أن يقال كيف بدلت جلود التذت بالمعاصي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r4.claim: Another view says the same skins return after burning, as bodies return after decay in graves; their difference is in condition, as when a ring is remade.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r4.anchor: والثاني أنها هي بعينها تعاد بعد احتراقها كما تعاد بعد البلى في القبور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r5.claim: Hasan al-Basri says the fire consumes them seventy thousand times each day; whenever it consumes them, they are told to return and do so.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p112#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري في هذه الآية تأكلهم النار كل يوم سبعين ألف مرة كلما أكلتهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r1.claim: God will cast those who disbelieve His signs and turn from His messengers into a fire that envelops their whole bodies and every part.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r1.anchor: أي ندخلهم نارا دخولا يحيط بجميع أجرامهم، وأجزائهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r2.claim: Their punishment is continuous: when their skins are cooked, new skins replace them so they continue to taste torment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r2.anchor: ثم أخبر عن دوام عقوبتهم ونكالهم، فقال: {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها ليذوقوا العذاب}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash reports Ibn Umar's explanation that burned skins are replaced by white skins like sheets of paper.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r3.anchor: قال [الأعمش، عن ابن عمر] (2) إذا أحرقت جلودهم بدلوا جلودا بيضا أمثال القراطيس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r4.speaker: يحيى بن يزيد الحضرمي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Yazid says it reached him that a disbeliever has one hundred skins, with differently colored torments between each pair.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r4.anchor: وقال يحيى بن يزيد الحضرمي إنه بلغه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the fire cooks them seventy thousand times daily; Fudayl adds that after their flesh is consumed they are told to return, and they do.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r5.anchor: عن الحسن قوله: {كلما نضجت جلودهم [بدلناهم جلودا غيرها] (4) } الآية. قال: تنضجهم في اليوم سبعين ألف مرة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r6.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r6.claim: Muadh explains that the skins are replaced one hundred times in an hour; Umar confirms he heard this from the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r6.anchor: فقال معاذ بن جبل: عندي تفسيرها: تبدل في ساعة مائة مرة. فقال عمر: هكذا سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r7.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r7.claim: In Ibn Mardawayh's alternate account, Kaʿb says he read that skins are replaced one hundred twenty times in an hour; Umar confirms hearing this from the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p337/r7.anchor: فقال عمر: هكذا سمعت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r1.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says an earlier scripture described a person's skin as forty cubits, tooth as ninety cubits, and belly as large enough to contain a mountain; burned skin is replaced.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r1.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: مكتوب في الكتاب الأول أن جلد أحدهم أربعون ذراعا، وسنه تسعون ذراعا، وبطنه لو وضع فيه جبل لوسعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says people of Hell grow so large that the distance from an earlobe to a shoulder is seven hundred years, their skin is seventy cubits thick, and a tooth is like Mount Uhud; Ahmad alone transmits it by this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن ابن عمر، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يعظم أهل النار في النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir says the skins mean their garments, but Ibn Kathir rejects this as weak and contrary to the apparent meaning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p338/r3.anchor: وقيل: المراد بقوله: {كلما نضجت جلودهم} أي: سرابيلهم. حكاه ابن جرير، وهو ضعيف؛ لأنه خلاف الظاهر.

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r1.speaker: قراءة العامة
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r1.claim: The common reading has initial nun with damma from aslaytuhu, to cast someone into fire.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: نصليهم بضم النون من أصليته النار إصلاء إذا ألقيته فيها،

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r2.speaker: حميد ابن قيس
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r2.claim: Humayd ibn Qays reads with initial fatha, from salaytuhu, meaning roast them.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r2.anchor: وعن حميد ابن قيس بفتح النون من صليته صليا، أي يشويهم،

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r3.claim: Tabdil means change and may describe changed qualities while the entity remains, as when a ring is changed.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r3.anchor: التبديل: التغيير، والتبديل يطلق على تغيير الصفة، وإن كان العين باقيا بحاله، كما تقول: بدلت خاتمي،

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r4.claim: God may annihilate creation and restore it, calling it other even when substance remains; “the earth is changed” admits replacement or altered quality.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r4.anchor: وكما أنه تعالى يفني الخلق ثم يعيده فيجوز أن يقال: هذا غيره، وإن كان العين هو، وقد يكون التبديل بأن يوضع غيره موضعه، وقد قيل: في قوله: (يوم تبدل الأرض) الوجهان.

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r7.claim: Naran is the object on the damma reading; on fatha a preposition is omitted, meaning roast them with fire.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r7.anchor: نارا نصب لوقوع الفعل عليه على قراءة من قرأ بضم النون، تقديره: يلزمه نارا، وعلى فتح النون بنزع الخافضة،

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r11.claim: Discussion of believers and unbelievers is followed by their corresponding promise and threat.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r11.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر المؤمنين والكفار أعقبه بذكر الوعد والوعيد،

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r12.claim: Those rejecting God's proofs will be made to enter a fire that burns and punishes them.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r12.anchor: إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا أي جحدوا حجتنا سوف نصليهم نارا أي نلزمهم نارا نحرقهم ونعذبهم بها،

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r13.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r13.claim: Abu Muslim says the deniers themselves become fuel for the fire.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: نصيرهم وقودا لها عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r14.speaker: قتادة وجماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r14.claim: The first of four views takes the wording literally: as skins burn, new skins are supplied; the author calls this strongest.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r14.anchor: الأول: أنه يجدد لهم جلودا غير الجلود التي احترقت على ظاهر التلاوة، وهي في الحقيقة غيرها عن قتادة وجماعة من المفسرين وهو الأوجه،

JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r15.claim: The objection that replacement skin did not sin fails because punishment belongs to the living person, not independently to limbs or skin.
JISHUMI:v2p1598#2/r15.anchor: ولا يقال: إن الجلد المجدد لم يذنب، فكيف يعذب؟! وذلك لأن المعذب هو الحي، فلا اعتبار بالأطراف والجلود.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r1.claim: The construction means that God exchanged other skins for them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r1.anchor: أبدلناهم إياها فإن قلت كيف نعذب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r2.claim: New skins may be punished because punishment concerns the sensitive whole that sinned, not the skin in isolation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r2.anchor: العذاب للجملة الحساسة وهي التي عصت لا للجلد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r3.speaker: فضيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r3.claim: Al-Fuḍayl explains the renewal as making what has been cooked or scorched unscorched again.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r3.anchor: وعن فضيل يجعل النضيج غير نضيج

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r4.claim: A Prophetic report says their skins are replaced seven times each day; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r4.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( 285 ) ( تبدل جلودهم كل يوم سبع مرات )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r5.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the skins are replaced seventy times, becoming white like sheets of paper.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن : سبعين مرة يبدلون جلودا بيضاء كالقراطيس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r6.claim: The purpose clause means their experience of punishment continues without interruption, as in a wish that someone’s strength endure and increase.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r6.anchor: ليدوم لهم ذوقه ولا ينقطع . كقولك للعزيز : أعزك الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r7.claim: God is mighty because nothing He wills against the criminals can stop Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r7.anchor: لا يمتنع عليه شيء مما يريده بالمجرمين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r8.claim: God is wise because He punishes only with justice those who deserve punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p554#4/r8.anchor: لا يعذب إلا بعدل من يستحقه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r1.claim: One answer says pain reaches the person rather than skin and flesh; skin is burned only to convey pain, so its replacement does not change who is punished.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r1.anchor: ألم العذاب إنما يصل إلى الإنسان الذي هو غير الجلد واللحم , وإنما يحرق الجلد ليصل إلى الإنسان ألم العذاب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r2.claim: A second answer says the original skins are restored as new, unburned skins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r2.anchor: والجواب الثاني : أنه تعاد تلك الجلود الأولى جديدة [ غير ] محترقة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r3.claim: A third answer says the replacement skins are their garments before they were made clothing; the view rejects burned-then-restored skin because annihilation would bring relief, though the damned neither die nor have punishment eased.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p497/r3.anchor: أن الجلود المعادة إنما هي سرابيلهم من قبل أن جعلت لهم لباسا , فسماها الله جلودا

MUQATIL:4:56/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:56/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:56/r1.claim: The disbelievers here are the Jews, and God's signs are the Qurʾān.
MUQATIL:4:56/r1.anchor: ثم أخبر بمستقر الكفار، فقال سبحانه: { إن الذين كفروا } ، يعنى اليهود، { بآياتنا } ، يعنى القرآن،

MUQATIL:4:56/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:56/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:56/r2.claim: Their skins “ripen” means they are burned by the fire.
MUQATIL:4:56/r2.anchor: { سوف نصليهم نارا كلما نضجت } ، يعنى احترقت { جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها } ،

MUQATIL:4:56/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:56/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:56/r3.claim: When fire consumes their skins, God renews them seven times per day, each day measured by a day of this world, so they taste fresh punishment.
MUQATIL:4:56/r3.anchor: وذلك أن النار إذا أكلت جلودهم بدلت كل يوم سبع مرات على مقدار كل يوم من أيام الدنيا،

MUQATIL:4:56/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:56/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:56/r4.claim: God is mighty in His vengeance and wise because He decreed Hell for them.
MUQATIL:4:56/r4.anchor: { إن الله كان عزيزا } فى نقمته { حكيما } [آية:56 ]، حكم لهم النار.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r1.claim: Nuslīhim means We will make them enter the Fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r1.anchor: ﴿ إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم ﴾ ندخلهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r2.claim: The skin is burned and replaced by the same underlying skin in a different state, the view of Ahl al-Ḥaqq against the Karrāmiyya; Fudayl instead says the cooked becomes uncooked.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r2.anchor: فالتبديل والتغيير لتغاير الهيئتين لا لتغاير الأصلين عند أهل الحق خلافا للكرامية وعن فضيل يجعل النضيج غير نضيج

NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r3.claim: The purpose is that they keep tasting torment without interruption, as in the wish may God keep you in your honor.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r3.anchor: ليدوم لهم ذوقه ولا ينقطع كقولك للعزيز أعزك الله أى أدامك على عزك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r4.claim: God is unconquerable in exacting vengeance, with none able to prevent what He wills against sinners, and wise in what He does to disbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p228/r4.anchor: ﴿ إن الله كان عزيزا ﴾ غالبا بالانتقام لا يمتنع عليه شيء مما يريده بالمجرمين ﴿ حكيما ﴾ فيما يفعل بالكافرين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r1.speaker: حميد بن قيس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r1.claim: Hamid ibn Qays reads naṣlīhim with an open initial nun, meaning ‘We roast them,’ as in the expression for a roasted sheep.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r1.anchor: وقرأ حميد بن قيس «نصليهم» بفتح النون أي نشويهم. يقال: شاة مصلية.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r2.claim: On this reading, nāran is accusative through omission of a preposition, with the sense ‘in a fire.’
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r2.anchor: ونصب «نارا» على هذه القراءة بنزع الخافض تقديره بنار.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r3.claim: Nadija means to become cooked; nadij al-ra’y describes sound judgment. Here skins are replaced with other skins.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r3.anchor: يقال: نضج الشيء نضجا ونضجا، وفلان نضيج الرأي محكمه. والمعنى في الآية: تبدل الجلود جلودا أخر.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r4.claim: Against the objection that a non-sinning skin is punished, al-Qurtubi says the skin itself is not punished: souls perceive the pain, and changing skins increases their torment.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r4.anchor: قيل له: ليس الجلد بمعذب ولا معاقب، وإنما الألم واقع على النفوس لأنها هي التي تحس وتعرف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r5.claim: ‘So they may taste the torment’ supports the role of souls in feeling pain; 17:97 says that when the Fire abates, its blaze is increased.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r5.anchor: يدل عليه قوله تعالى: { ليذوقوا العذاب } وقوله تعالى: كلما خبت زدناهم سعيرا [الإسراء: 97].

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r6.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r6.claim: Muqatil says the Fire consumes them seven times each day.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r6.anchor: مقاتل: تأكله النار كل يوم سبع مرات.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says this happens seventy thousand times; whenever they are consumed, they are told to return and return as they were.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r7.anchor: الحسن: سبعين ألف مرة كلما أكلتهم قيل لهم: عودوا فعادوا كما كانوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r8.claim: Ibn Umar says that after burning, they receive white skins like sheets of paper.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r8.anchor: ابن عمر: إذا احترقوا بدلت لهم جلود بيض كالقراطيس.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r9.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r9.claim: One interpretation takes the skins as garments, comparing 14:49–50; garments are called skins because they cling to the body, and each burned garment is renewed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r9.anchor: وقيل: عنى بالجلود السرابيل كما قال تعالى: وترى المجرمين يومئذ مقرنين في الأصفاد [إبراهيم:49] سرابيلهم من قطران

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r10.claim: Ibn Umar’s poem calls Salim the ‘skin between the eye and nose,’ illustrating the close attachment meant by skin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r10.anchor: وأنشد ابن عمر رضي الله عنه: يلومونني في سالم وألومهم وجلدة بين العين والأنف سالم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r11.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r11.claim: A poet calls the Banu Taym’s green garments their skins, supporting the garment interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r11.anchor: قال الشاعر: كسا اللؤم تيما خضرة في جلودها فويل لتيم من سرابيلها الخضر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r12.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r12.claim: Another view says the original skin is renewed in a changed state, like a jeweler recasting the same ring; ‘other’ is figurative because the underlying material remains the same.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r12.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أعدنا الجلد الأول جديدا كما تقول للصائغ: صغ لي من هذا الخاتم خاتما غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r13.claim: The analogy extends to a soul recreated after becoming dust and a familiar brother whose condition changes while he remains himself.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57/r13.anchor: وهذا كالنفس إذا صارت ترابا وصارت لا شيء ثم أحياها الله تعالى: وكعهدك بأخ لك صحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r1.claim: In 14:48 the earth remains the same despite changed hills, mountains, rivers, and trees, and being widened and leveled.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r1.anchor: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض [إبراهيم: 48] وهي تلك الأرض بعينها إلا أنها تغير آكامها وجبالها وأنهارها وأشجارها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r2.claim: A poet says people and a house are no longer as he knew them, describing changed conditions rather than new entities.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r2.anchor: ومن هذا المعنى قول الشاعر: فما الناس بالناس الذين عهدتهم ولا الدار بالدار التي كنت أعرف

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi relates Ibn Abbas’s response to Aisha’s lament, quoting Labid; Ibn Abbas says ʿAd also lamented its age, and a spear found long after its destruction bore a verse about changed conditions though the land remained.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r3.anchor: وقال الشعبي: جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس فقال: ألا ترى ما صنعت عائشة! ذمت دهرها، وأنشدت بيتي لبيد:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r4.claim: Al-ʿAziz means nothing can overcome or elude God; al-Hakim describes His wisdom in threatening servants.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:56-57#2/r4.anchor: { إن الله كان عزيزا } أي لا يعجزه شيء ولا يفوته. { حكيما } في إيعاده عباده.

QASHANI:4:56/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:56/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:56/r1.claim: Disbelief in the signs means being veiled from God’s manifestations in attributes and acts; the passage opens with His manifestation through knowledge, wisdom, and sovereignty in Abraham’s household.

QASHANI:4:56/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:56/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:56/r2.claim: One possible fire is the longing for perfection demanded by their natures and capacities while their veil remains firmly rooted.
QASHANI:4:56/r2.anchor: نار شوق الكمال لاقتضاء غرائزهم وطبائعهم بحسب استعدادهم ذلك مع رسوخ الحجاب ولزومه

QASHANI:4:56/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:56/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:56/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is the fire of coercion arising from manifestations of God’s overpowering attributes, in a form suited to their states.
QASHANI:4:56/r3.anchor: نار قهر من تجليات صفات قهره تناسب أحوالهم

QASHANI:4:56/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:56/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:56/r4.claim: A third reading makes the fire their own evil selves and the intense craving for qualities and pleasures they were habituated to but are denied.
QASHANI:4:56/r4.anchor: نار شره نفوسهم وحدة شوقها وطلبها لما ضريت بها من كمالات صفاتها وشهواتها مع حرمانها عنها

QASHANI:4:56/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:56/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:56/r5.claim: As they shed bodily coverings, those veils are lifted and replaced by new ones, so they continue tasting the fires of deprivation.
QASHANI:4:56/r5.anchor: حجبا غيرها جديدة { ليذوقوا العذاب } نيران الحرمان

QASHANI:4:56/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:56/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:56/r6.claim: God’s might subdues and humiliates them through their own soul-qualities, burning them with longing for perfections they are forever denied.
QASHANI:4:56/r6.anchor: قويا يقهرهم ويذلهم بذل صفات نفوسهم

QASHANI:4:56/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:56/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:56/r7.claim: God’s wisdom gives them punishment suited to what they chose through angry and appetitive impulses and their attraction to bodily pleasures, exchanging one dark veil for another.
QASHANI:4:56/r7.anchor: يجازيهم بما يناسبهم من العذاب الذي اختاروه لأنفسهم

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r1.claim: After threatening a particular group among the People of the Book, the passage states the threat that applies to disbelievers generally.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r1.anchor: بعدما ذكر الوعيد بالطائفة الخاصة من أهل الكتاب بين ما يعم الكافرين من الوعيد

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r2.claim: God’s signs include everything indicating His essence, acts, attributes, and names, as well as angels, scriptures, and messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r2.anchor: يدخل في الآيات كل ما يدل على ذات الله وأفعاله وصفاته وأسمائه والملائكة والكتب والرسل

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r3.claim: Disbelief in the signs can mean denying their status as signs, neglecting to consider them, raising doubts about them, or knowingly rejecting them out of obstinacy and envy; Rāzī discussed disbelief at 2:6.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r3.anchor: وكفرهم بالآيات ليس يكون بالجحد ، لكن بوجوه ، منها أن ينكروا كونها آيات ، ومنها أن يغفلوا عنها

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh says sawfa signals threat and warning, with sīn serving similarly; it can also introduce promises, but both particles are specific to the future.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه : ( سوف ) كلمة تذكر للتهديد والوعيد ، يقال : سوف أفعل ، وينوب عنها حرف السين

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r5.claim: Nuṣlīhim means to make them enter the Fire and also carries the added sense of roasting them, as one says a roasted sheep.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r5.anchor: قوله : { نصليهم } أي ندخلهم النار ، لكن قوله : { نصليهم } فيه زيادة على ذلك فانه بمنزلة شويته بالنار ، يقال شاة مصلية أي مشوية

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r6.claim: Asked why God does not preserve their bodies from burning, Rāzī answers that God is not questioned about His acts and can inflict immense pain without fire, though He places them in fire.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r6.anchor: أنه تعالى لا يسأل عما يفعل ، بل نقول : انه تعالى قادر على أن يوصل إلى أبدانهم آلاما عظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r7.claim: Rāzī raises the justice objection that replacing burned skin with new skin would punish skin that did not commit the sin.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#2/r7.anchor: هذا تعذيبا لمن لم يعص وهو غير جائز .

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r1.claim: One answer treats ripeness as a changed attribute of the same skin-subject, so the person punished remains the same and the change is only in quality.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r1.anchor: أن يجعل النضج غير النضيج ، فالذات واحدة والمتبدل هو الصفة

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r2.claim: Another answer says the human being is punished and skin is an attached addition, not part of the human essence; renewing it therefore does not punish someone else.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r2.anchor: المعذب هو الإنسان ، وذلك الجلد ما كان جزأ من ماهية الإنسان ، بل كان كالشيء الملتصق به

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r3.claim: A third interpretation takes skins as garments, so their renewal refers to clothing; it cites the garments of tar in 14:50.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r3.anchor: أن المراد بالجلود السرابيل ، قال تعالى : { سرابيلهم من قطران } ( إبراهيم : 50 )

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī rejects the garment interpretation as abandoning the apparent wording and says tar garments are described as burning, not ripening.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r4.anchor: طعن القاضي فيه ، فقال : إنه ترك للظاهر ، وأيضا السرابيل من القطران لا توصف بالنضج

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r5.claim: A fourth possibility reads the skin renewal as a metaphor for unending torment: whenever the damned seem to have reached death, they receive renewed life and suffering continues.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r5.anchor: هذا استعارة عن الدوام وعدم الانقطاع ، كما يقال لمن يراد وصفه بالدوام : كلما انتهى فقد ابتدأ

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r6.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says God makes replacement skin from the unbeliever’s own flesh; Rāzī calls this unlikely because the finite flesh would eventually run out and another mechanism is not explained.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r6.anchor: قال السدي : إنه تعالى يبدل الجلود من لحم الكافر فيخرج من لحمه جلدا آخر وهذا بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r7.claim: Li-yadhūqū means that their tasting of punishment continues without interruption, like a wish that someone remain in and increase in honor.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r7.anchor: أي ليدوم لهم ذوقه ولا ينقطع ، كقولك للمعزوز : أعزك الله ، أي أدامك على العز وزادك فيه

RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r8.claim: The phrase can also mean they taste the punishment in their renewed state, since they are already continuously tasting it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p108#3/r8.anchor: وأيضا المراد ليذوقوا بهذه الحالة الجديدة العذاب ، وإلا فهم ذائقون مستمرون عليه

STUDYQURAN:4:56/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r1.claim: Repeated consumption and replacement of Hell’s skins conveys punishment continuing without end.
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r1.anchor: The image of the skins of those in Hell being consumed

STUDYQURAN:4:56/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r2.claim: Some commentators take the Quran’s afterlife pleasures and torments literally rather than as metaphors for spiritual reward and punishment.
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r2.anchor: understood by some commentators as suggesting that the pleasures and torments of the Afterlife as described in the Quran are meant to be taken literally

STUDYQURAN:4:56/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r3.speaker: other commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r3.claim: Others read “skins” as garments of pitch worn in Hell; as they burn, they are replaced so the condemned can be set alight again.
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r3.anchor: Others say that skins refers to the garments made of pitch (14:50) that those in Hell will wear

STUDYQURAN:4:56/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r4.claim: The renewal has also been understood as changing the attributes of those in Hell without changing their essence.
STUDYQURAN:4:56/r4.anchor: The constant renewal of their skins has also been understood as indicating a continuous change in the attributes of those in Hell without any change in their essence

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r1.claim: This is a threat to Jews of the Children of Israel and other unbelievers who persist in denying what God revealed to Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r1.anchor: هذا وعيد من الله جل ثناؤه للذين أقاموا على تكذيبهم بما أنزل الله على محمد

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r2.claim: God's signs here are the signs of revelation and the proofs in His revealed book that establish Muhammad's truth.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r2.anchor: من آياتي، يعني من آيات تنزيله ووحي كتابه، وهي دلالاته وحججه على صدق محمد

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r3.claim: To be made to enter the fire means to be roasted and scorched in it.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r3.anchor: سوف ننضجهم في نار يصلون فيها: أي يشوون فيها

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r4.claim: Whenever their skins are scorched and burned, God replaces them with skins other than those that have been burned.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r4.anchor: يقول: كلما انشوت بها جلودهم فاحترقت {بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء: 56]

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r5.claim: Ibn Umar says that when the skins burn, they are replaced with white skins like sheets of paper.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر: {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء: 56] قال: «إذا احترقت جلودهم

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r6.claim: Qatada paraphrases the cycle as replacing the skins whenever they burn.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم نارا كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء: 56]

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r7.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabi reports that an earlier scripture gives the unbeliever's skin as forty cubits, height as seventy cubits, and belly as large enough for a mountain; burned skins are replaced.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r7.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {كلما نضجت جلودهم} [النساء: 56] قال: «سمعنا أنه مكتوب في الكتاب الأول أن جلد أحدهم أربعون ذراعا

TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r8.claim: A report from al-Hasan says God roasts them seventy thousand times in a day.
TAB-FULL:v7p162#2/r8.anchor: عن الحسن: {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء: 56] قال: «ننضجهم في اليوم سبعين ألف مرة»

TAB-FULL:v7p165/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the fire burns seventy thousand skins each day and that an unbeliever's skin is forty cubits thick, with God knowing which cubit is meant.
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قوله: {كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها} [النساء: 56] قال: «تنضج النار كل يوم سبعين ألف جلد

TAB-FULL:v7p165/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r2.claim: One view says pain belongs to the person apart from skin and flesh; these do not feel pain, so innumerable new skins may be created and burned to make the person feel it.
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم: العذاب إنما يصل إلى الأنسان الذي هو غير الجلد واللحم، وإنما يحرق الجلد ليصل إلى الإنسان ألم العذاب

TAB-FULL:v7p165/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r3.claim: Another view says skin, flesh, and all body parts feel pain; the same skin is restored unburned after burning, like a ring remade by a goldsmith and called another ring.
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل الجلود تألم , واللحم وسائر أجزاء جسم بني آدم، وإذا أحرق جلده أو غيره من أجزاء جسده

TAB-FULL:v7p165/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r4.speaker: آخرون
