TAB-FULL:v7p165/r4.claim: A further view takes the skins to mean pitch garments that cling so closely to their wearers that they are called their skins; when they burn, other pitch garments replace them.
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: {كلما نضجت جلودهم} [النساء: 56] سرابيلهم، بدلناهم سرابيل من قطران غيرها.

TAB-FULL:v7p165/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r5.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r5.claim: Proponents of the garment view say the unbelievers' bodily skins do not burn away, since that would end in death and relief; God says they do not die, so no body part ceases to exist.
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r5.anchor: قالوا: وأما جلود أهل الكفر من أهل النار فإنها لا تحرق، لأن في احتراقها إلى حال إعادتها فناءها

TAB-FULL:v7p165/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r6.claim: The replacements make them experience the pain, distress, and severity of punishment for their denial and rejection of God's signs in worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v7p165/r6.anchor: فعلنا ذلك بهم ليجدوا ألم العذاب وكربه وشدته بما كانوا في الدنيا يكذبون آيات الله

SULAMI:v1p150#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p150#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p150#2/r1.claim: One gloss reads the verse as God's making clarification manifest to the elect.
SULAMI:v1p150#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم رحمه الله : بإظهار البيان على الخواص

TABRISI:4:56-57/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r1.claim: The verb aṣlāhu means to cast someone into fire; ṣalāhu means to roast him, and ṣilāʾ is roasting.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r1.anchor: يقال أصليته النار إذا ألقيته فيها، وصليته صليا إذا شويته، وشاة مصلية مشوية

TABRISI:4:56-57/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r2.claim: The idiom ṣalā fulān bi-sharr fulān means that someone suffered another’s evil.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r2.anchor: والصلاء: الشواء. وصلى فلان بشر فلان، والتبديل التغيير

TABRISI:4:56-57/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r3.claim: Tabdīl may replace one entity with another; the cited line “the prince replaced by the prince” illustrates substitution.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r3.anchor: أبدلت الشيء بالشيء إذا أزلت عينا بعين كما قال الشاعر: عزل الأمير بالأمير المبدل

TABRISI:4:56-57/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r4.speaker: المغربي
TABRISI:4:56-57/r4.claim: With a doubled dāl, baddala can change an object’s form while its substance remains, as in changing a cloak into a shirt.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r4.anchor: والعين واحدة. يقولون: بدلت جبتي قميصا أي جعلتها قميصا ذكره المغربي

TABRISI:4:56-57/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r5.claim: Tabdīl can also mean putting something else in an object's place, as in the earth being changed for another earth.

TABRISI:4:56-57/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r6.speaker: رؤية
TABRISI:4:56-57/r6.claim: Ruʾya says shade is where the sun has been and then departs; elsewhere only ẓill applies, including the night’s shelter from the sun.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r6.anchor: رؤية كل موضع تكون فيه الشمس

TABRISI:4:56-57/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r7.claim: Ẓulla means a covering or canopy, and ẓalīl describes something sheltered.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r7.anchor: والظل الليل كأنه كالستر من الشمس

TABRISI:4:56-57/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r8.claim: After discussing believers and unbelievers, the passage sets out the promise and threat attached to faith and unbelief.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r8.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر المؤمن والكافر عقبه بذكر الوعد والوعيد على الإيمان والكفر

TABRISI:4:56-57/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r9.claim: Those who disbelieve in God’s signs deny His proofs, call His prophets liars, and reject signs of His oneness and the Prophet’s truth.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r9.anchor: أي جحدوا حججنا وكذبوا أنبياءنا ودفعوا الآيات الدالة على توحدنا وصدق نبينا

TABRISI:4:56-57/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r10.claim: God will consign them to a fire that burns and tortures them; sawfa marks this as future action.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r10.anchor: أي نلزمهم نارا نحرقهم فيها، ونعذبهم بها، ودخلت سوف لتدل على أنه يفعل ذلك بهم

TABRISI:4:56-57/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r11.speaker: قتادة وجماعة من أهل التفسير
TABRISI:4:56-57/r11.claim: The apparent wording means God renews their skins with genuinely different skins; Qatada and other exegetes report this, and Ali ibn ʿIsa chooses it.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r11.anchor: على ظاهر القرآن في أنها غيرها عن قتادة وجماعة من أهل التفسير واختاره علي بن عيسى

TABRISI:4:56-57/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r12.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:4:56-57/r12.claim: Ali ibn ʿIsa answers that only the living person is punished; the added skin does not itself feel pain but conveys pain to the one who deserves it.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r12.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى: إن ما يزاد لا يؤلم ولا هو بعض لما يؤلم وإنما هو شيء يصل به الألم

TABRISI:4:56-57/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r13.speaker: الزجاج والبلخي وأبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:4:56-57/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj, al-Balkhi, and Abu ʿAli al-Jubbaʾi say the same skin is restored to its unburned state; this avoids punishing an innocent new body.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r13.anchor: وثانيها: أن الله يجددها بأن يردها إلى الحالة التي كانت عليها غير محترقة

TABRISI:4:56-57/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r14.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:56-57/r14.claim: A third view says the garments of tar are meant by “skins” through contiguity; al-Tabrisi rejects this as leaving the apparent meaning without evidence.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r14.anchor: وثالثها: أن التبديل إنما هو للسرابيل التي ذكرها الله تعالى سرابيلهم من قطران

TABRISI:4:56-57/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r15.claim: Those who regard the true human being as other than the observed bodily aggregate avoid the objection about punishing someone who did not commit the sin.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r15.anchor: فأما من قال: إن الإنسان غير هذه الجملة المشاهدة وأنه المعذب في الحقيقة

TABRISI:4:56-57/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r16.claim: “Taste the punishment” means feel its pain; renewed skin makes pain begin afresh in each state, unlike pain that grows easier through habituation.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r16.anchor: معناه ليجدوا ألم العذاب وإنما قال ذلك ليبين أنهم كالمبتدأ عليهم العذاب في كل حالة

TABRISI:4:56-57/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57/r17.claim: ʿAzīz means always mighty and unassailable, with no one able to resist or thwart God.
TABRISI:4:56-57/r17.anchor: أي لم يزل منيعا لا يدافع ولا يمانع

TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r1.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r1.claim: An alternative gloss says God is able to carry out whatever He threatens or promises.
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه قادر لا يمتنع عليه إنجاز ما توعد به أو وعده

TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r2.claim: God is wise in His management, determination, and punishment of those He punishes.
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r2.anchor: { حكيما } في تدبيره وتقديره وفي تعذيب من يعذبه

TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reports that their skins are cooked through seventy thousand times each day.
TABRISI:4:56-57#2/r3.anchor: روى الكلبي عن الحسن قال: بلغنا أن جلودهم تنضج كل يوم سبعين ألف مرة

THALABI:v3p329/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p329/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p329/r9.claim: The author explains سوف نصليهم نارا as We shall put them into a fire.
THALABI:v3p329/r9.anchor: إن الذين كفروا بآياتنا سوف نصليهم نارا ندخلهم نارا،

THALABI:v3p329/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p329/r10.speaker: حميد بن قيس
THALABI:v3p329/r10.claim: Hamid ibn Qays reads the verb with fatḥa on the nūn; the author glosses this as making them roast, while another gloss equates it with putting them in the fire.
THALABI:v3p329/r10.anchor: وقرأ حميد بن قيس: نصليهم بفتح النون: أي نسويهم، وقيل: معناه نصليهم.

THALABI:v3p329/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p329/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p329/r11.claim: On Hamid's reading, نارا is accusative with a dropped preposition, understood as بنار.
THALABI:v3p329/r11.anchor: فنصب نارا على هذه القراءة بنزع الخافض تقديره بنار.

THALABI:v3p330/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p330/r1.claim: The replaced skins are the burnt skins; Ibn Abbas describes the replacement as white like sheets of paper.
THALABI:v3p330/r1.anchor: كلما نضجت (جلودهم) بدلناهم جلودا غيرها غير الجلود المحترقة.

THALABI:v3p330/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p330/r2.claim: Umar heard the Prophet say that the skins are replaced one hundred times in an hour; Muadh supplied this interpretation after Umar asked for the verse to be repeated.
THALABI:v3p330/r2.anchor: قال معاذ بن جبل: عندي تفسيرها: بدلت في ساعة مائة مرة؟، قال عمر: هكذا سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول.

THALABI:v3p330/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v3p330/r3.claim: Hasan says the fire consumes them seventy thousand times each day; each time they are told to return, they return as they were.
THALABI:v3p330/r3.anchor: هشام عن الحسن في قوله تعالى: كلما نضجت جلودهم بدلناهم جلودا غيرها قال: تأكلهم كل يوم سبعين ألف مرة

THALABI:v3p330/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v3p330/r4.claim: Mujahid says worms lie between the skin, flesh, and blood, and the skin is extended like the hide of a wild ass.
THALABI:v3p330/r4.anchor: المسيب عن الأعمش عن مجاهد قال: ما بين جلده ولحمه ودمه دود فأجلدت كجلدة حمر الوحش.

THALABI:v3p330/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p330/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a disbeliever's skin is forty-two cubits thick and his molar is like Mount Uhud.
THALABI:v3p330/r5.anchor: الأعمش عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «غلظ جلد الكافر اثنان وأربعون ذراعا وضرسه مثل أحد»

THALABI:v3p330/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p330/r6.claim: The author answers that the person, not skin in isolation, sins and suffers; skins feel pain through spirits, and the wording says they taste the punishment.
THALABI:v3p330/r6.anchor: قلنا: إن المعاصي والألم واقع على نفس. الإنسان لا الجلد، لأن الجلود إنما تألم بالأرواح،

THALABI:v3p330/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r7.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v3p330/r7.claim: An alternative says the replacement skins are the same skins after their condition changes; غير can mark alteration without making something wholly other, like a silver ring recast from itself.
THALABI:v3p330/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه: يبدل جلودا هي تلك الجلود المحترقة، وذلك أن غير على ضربين: غير تضاد،

THALABI:v3p330/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p330/r8.claim: The author analogizes the same person in changed condition and links this sense of replacement to the earth being changed while remaining that same earth.
THALABI:v3p330/r8.anchor: ونظير هذا قوله تعالى يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض وهي تلك الأرض بعينها إلا أنها قد بدلت

THALABI:v3p330/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r9.speaker: لبيد
THALABI:v3p330/r9.claim: A cited poem illustrates how people and dwellings cease to be as they once were, echoing the argument that identity persists through changed condition.
THALABI:v3p330/r9.anchor: فما الناس بالناس الذين عهدتهم … ولا الدار بالدار التي كنت أعرف

THALABI:v3p330/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p330/r10.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v3p330/r10.claim: A report reaching al-Sha'bi says a man complained to Ibn Abbas that Aisha disparaged time by reciting two lines of Labid; the excerpt ends before the lines or Ibn Abbas's answer.
THALABI:v3p330/r10.anchor: سمعت الشعبي يقول: جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس فقال: ألا ترى ما صنعت عائشة ذمت دهرها وذلك [أنها] أنشدت بيتي لبيد:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r1.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r1.claim: Sibawayh calls sawfa a particle of respite, threat, and warning; he also notes the form saw without fāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r1.anchor: سيبويه: سوف أداة تنفيس وتهديد ووعيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r2.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r2.claim: Another view derives sawfa from postponement: “I will give you” means later, not now; sīn can replace it. This reading takes the threat as future punishment and cites 74:26 and 93:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: هي أداة التسويف، كأنها مأخوذة منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r3.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r3.claim: Some call sawfa a particle of causation, consequence, or confirmation; in 12:98, Joseph's promise is said to defer supplication until dawn to secure it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: سوف كلمة تعليل، وهي أيضا كلمة العقبى كهي في هذه الآية، وكلمة تحقيق أيضا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r4.claim: The author refers to earlier discussions of iṣlāʾ at 4:10 and “they will burn in a blazing fire.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r4.anchor: وذكرنا ما في الإصلاء عند قوله: {وسيصلون سعيرا} [النساء: 10]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says their replacement skins are white, like sheets of paper.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يبدلون جلودا بيضا كأمثال القراطيس (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r6.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r6.claim: Muʿadh ibn Jabal says the skins are replaced one hundred times in an hour; the report is also transmitted as a Prophetic report through ʿUmar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r6.anchor: وقال معاذ بن جبل (¬4): يبدل في ساعة مائة مرة. وروى ذلك مرفوعا عمر عن النبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r7.speaker: جماعة من أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r7.claim: A group of language scholars, including al-Zajjaj, Ibn Kaysan, and Ibn al-Anbari, say that once the skins are cooked they are renewed to their unburned state; “other” can describe a changed form while the underlying substance remains the same.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r7.anchor: قال جماعة من أهل المعاني: إن جلودهم إذا نضجت واحترقت جددت، بأن ترد إلى الحال التي كانت عليها غير محترقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ illustrates two uses of baddala: replacing a ring with another object, and melting the ring into a hoop; in the latter, its material remains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p527/r8.anchor: قال الفراء: بدلت الخاتم بالحلقة إذا نحيت هذا وجعلت هذا مكانه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r1.speaker: أبو العباس أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r1.claim: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya says tabdīl changes one form into another while preserving the same substance; ibdāl removes the original substance and substitutes a new one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r1.anchor: قال أبو العباس: وحقيقته أن التبديل تغيير صورة إلى صورة أخرى، والجوهرة (¬4) بعينها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r2.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Arabs sometimes use baddala for abdala, as in 25:70, where sins are removed and replaced by good deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r2.anchor: قد جعلت العرب بدلت بمعنى أبدلت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r3.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad applies the form-change sense here: the substance of the skin remains, but after blackening in torment its original form is restored; the author says this is supported by Ibn Abbas's report.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r3.anchor: وهذه هي الجوهرة بعينها باقية، وتبديلها تغيير صورتها إلى غيرها؛ لأنها كانت ناعمة فاسودت بالعذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r4.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says baddala and abdala cannot be distinguished: in 16:101 the replaced verse may remain recited or be lifted, while in 34:16 both gardens remain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r4.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: ليس ينفصل (بدل) من (أبدل) بشيء، فقد يقال: تبدل في الشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r5.speaker: جماعة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r5.claim: Some take the wording literally: God creates new skins and removes the burned ones. They answer the objection that an unoffending skin is punished by saying the skin does not feel; the person does, as “so they may taste the punishment” says. Here ghayr means different in an incompatible sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r5.anchor: ومنهم من أجرى الآية على ظاهرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r6.claim: Abu Bakr says God clothes them in skins that transmit pain to their souls and hearts without themselves feeling it; he compares them to the tar garments in 14:50.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r6.anchor: واعتمد أبو بكر (¬4) هذا القول فقال: إن الله تعالى يلبسهم جلودا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r7.speaker: أبو النجم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r7.claim: Abu al-Najm's line about the prince replacing another prince illustrates exchanging one body for another, the sense of ibdāl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p529/r7.anchor: ومنه قول أبي النجم: عزل الأمير للأمير المبدل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r1.speaker: بعضهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r1.claim: A more remote interpretation takes the skins as the tar garments of 14:50, called skins because they cling against the body.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r1.anchor: ومنهم من أبعد في التأويل فقال: أراد بالجلود السرابيل في قوله: {سرابيلهم من قطران}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r2.claim: The expression “skin” can name something closely associated with a person, as in a cited line about the skin between eye and nose.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r3.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r3.claim: An anonymous poet calls garments “skins” in a line about Taim's green garments, supporting the adjacency interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r3.anchor: وينشد على هذا قول الشاعر: كسا اللؤم تيما خضرة في جلودها ... فويل لتيم من سرابيلها الخضر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says a disbeliever's skin turns back into flesh and a new skin emerges from the flesh, so no skin that did not commit sin is substituted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r4.anchor: وللسدي في هذا مذهب آخر، هو أنه قال: تبدل الجلود جلودا غيرها من لحم الكافر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r5.claim: Naḍija means softened by heat, short of being burned through.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r5.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {كلما نضجت} أي لانت، والنضج هو اللين بالحرارة، وهو دون الاحتراق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r6.claim: Naḍija is more forceful than “burned”: a fully burned skin cannot feel, and a pause between its destruction and renewal would relieve the unbeliever, whereas 2:162 says their punishment is not lightened or deferred.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p531/r6.anchor: ولفظ النضج ههنا أبلغ في التعذيب من لفظ الإحراق؛ لأنها إذا احترقت لم تحس بألم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r1.claim: The repeated tasting metaphor conveys renewed sensation each time, without any loss of feeling despite the punishment's severity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r1.anchor: استعمل لفظ الذوق ههنا مع عظم ما نالوا من شدة العذاب إخبارا بأن إحساسهم به في كل حال كإحساس الذائق في تجديد الوجدان من غير نقصان في الإحساس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r2.claim: Dhāq means to taste; dhawāq and madhāq can mean either verbal nouns or taste/flavor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r2.anchor: ويقال: ذاق يذوق ذوقا ومذاقا وذواقا، والذواق والمذاق يكونان مصدرين ويكونان طعما، كما تقول: ذواقه ومذاقه طيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r3.claim: Taste can be perceived by the mouth and by other parts of the body.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r3.anchor: وروى ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي قال: الذوق يكون بالفم وبغير الفم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r4.claim: God is powerful, none can overcome Him, and He is wise in what He ordains.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p533/r4.anchor: أي هو قوي لا يغلبه شيء، وهو مع ذلك حكيم فيما دبر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r1.claim: When their skins are burned through, they are renewed to their former unburned condition.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r1.anchor: يعني: أن جلودهم إذا نضجت واحترقت جددت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r2.claim: To taste the punishment means to undergo and experience it.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r3.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is powerful and none can overcome Him; He is wise in what He ordains.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:56-58/r3.anchor: قويا لا يغلبه شيء { حكيما } فيما دبر

MAJAZ:v1p129/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p129/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p129/r10.claim: Nuṣlīhim means roast and cook them in fire; a maṣliyya sheep was described as roasted, including in the report of a Jewish woman gifting one to the Prophet.
MAJAZ:v1p129/r10.anchor: نصليهم نارا» (56) : نشويهم بالنار وننضجهم بها، يقال: أتانا بحمل مصلى مشوى، وذكروا أن يهودية أهدت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شاة مصلية

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r1.claim: The commentary says knowledge of the body shows that nerves carrying pain to the brain are in membranes and skin, not internal organs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r1.anchor: İnsan bedeniyle ilgili bilgiler arttıkça acıyı beyne ulaştıran sinirlerin iç organlarda değil, zarlarda ve deride olduğu anlaşılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r2.claim: If skin vanished during a long or eternal burning, the person would no longer feel pain; replacing it expresses that no such escape is possible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r2.anchor: Uzun zaman veya ebediyen yanacak olan bir bedenin derisi yok olsaydı sahibi yanma acısını duyamaz hale gelirdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r3.claim: The body transmits pleasure and pain to soul and consciousness; changing the body or a body part does not change the person while the self, spirit, and consciousness remain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r3.anchor: Beden ruha ve şuura haz ve elemi ulaştıran bir vasıtadan ibarettir. Kişinin nefsi, ruhu ve şuuru değişmedikçe bedenin veya bir parçasının değişmesi kişinin de değişmesini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r4.claim: It is mistaken to call renewed-skin punishment unjust because the skin is innocent: the enduring person, soul, and consciousness suffer, not skin by itself.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:56/r4.anchor: ileri sürmek yanlış anlama ve değerlendirme ile eksik bilgiye dayanmaktadır; çünkü acı çeken deri değil, insanın kendisi; değişmeyen ruhu ve şuurudur.

BAQILLANI:v1p108/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r1.speaker: من الأدباء
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r1.claim: Some critics said Abu Tammam's pursuit of badiʿ drained his poetry of its natural force; Ahmad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ammar went further and disparaged his merits.
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r1.anchor: من الأدباء من عاب عليه هذه الأبيات ونحوها على ما قد تكلف فيها من البديع وتعمل من الصنعة

BAQILLANI:v1p108/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r2.claim: Excessive love of artifice led Abu Tammam to ugly metaphors and strained lines, with examples of grotesque comparisons and wordplay.
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r2.anchor: فهذا من الاستعارات القبيحة والبديع المقيت

BAQILLANI:v1p108/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r3.claim: Abu Tammam's repeated antithesis, paronomasia, metaphor, and other devices can make his verse heavy and forced, though an occasional line is graceful.
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r3.anchor: حتى استثقل نظمه واستوخم رصفه وكان التكلف باردا والتصرف جامدا وربما اتفق مع ذلك في كلامه النادر المليح

BAQILLANI:v1p108/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r4.claim: Al-Buhturi uses paronomasia less than Abu Tammam; his antithesis is often graceful, and his pursuit of smoothness usually keeps his craft free of faults.
BAQILLANI:v1p108/r4.anchor: وأما البحتري فإنه لا يرى في التجنيس ما يراه أبو تمام ويقل التصنع له فإذا وقع في كلامه كان في الأكثر حسنا رشيقا

BURHAN:v4p324/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p324/r1.claim: Here ما is temporal-source, standing with its clause in place of a time adverb; the sense is every time, though ما itself is not a time adverb.
BURHAN:v4p324/r1.anchor: وهذه تسمى ما المصدرية الظرفية أي النائبة عن الظرف لا أنها ظرف في نفسها

BURHAN:v4p324/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p324/r2.claim: كل is accusative as an adverb because it is annexed to an expression functioning in place of a time adverb.
BURHAN:v4p324/r2.anchor: ف كل من كلما منصوب على الظرفية لإضافته إلى شيء هو قائم مقام الظرف

BURHAN:v4p324/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BURHAN:v4p324/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says repetition comes from the universal force of temporal ما, while كل reinforces the generality already conveyed by the temporal construction.
BURHAN:v4p324/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو حيان وإنما ذلك من عموم ما لأن الظرفية مراد بها العموم

BURHAN:v4p324/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p324/r4.claim: Zarkashī rejects Abū Ḥayyān’s account: source ما is not general by itself, and its substitution for a time adverb does not make it so; the construction yields the generality.
BURHAN:v4p324/r4.anchor: وقوله إن التكرار من عموم ما ممنوع فإن ما المصدرية لا عموم لها ولا يلزم من نيابتها عن الظرف دلالتها

BURHAN:v4p324/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r5.speaker: بعض الأصوليين
BURHAN:v4p324/r5.claim: Some legal theorists say كلما intentionally generalizes actions but only implicitly generalizes nouns; without ما, the intended and implicit scopes reverse.
BURHAN:v4p324/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض الأصوليين أنها إذا وصلت ب ما صارت أداة لتكرار الأفعال وعمومها قصدي وفي الأسماء ضمنى

BURHAN:v4p324/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p324/r6.claim: With bare كل plus a noun, the example divorces each woman once, but marrying the same woman again does not trigger another divorce because nouns are not intentionally generalized through repeated acts.
BURHAN:v4p324/r6.anchor: كل أمرأة أتزوجها فهي طالق تطلق كل امرأة يتزوجها

BURHAN:v4p324/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p324/r7.claim: With كلما, repeated marriages to a woman trigger divorce each time, since the action of marrying is intentionally generalized.
BURHAN:v4p324/r7.anchor: كلما تزوجت امرأة فهى طالق فتزوج امرأة مرارا طلقت في كل مرة

BURHAN:v4p324/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r8.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p324/r8.claim: Sībawayh discusses كل as an adjective in the chapter on qualification, as in الرجل كل الرجل.
BURHAN:v4p324/r8.anchor: ذكره سيبويه في باب النعت قال ومن الصفة أنت الرجل كل الرجل

BURHAN:v4p324/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r9.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p324/r9.claim: Al-Ṣaffār says الرجل كل الرجل intensifies praise: الرجل means the complete man, and adding كل presents him as the man in his greatness, effectively standing for the whole genus.
BURHAN:v4p324/r9.anchor: قال الصفار هذا يكون عند قصد التأكيد والمبالغة فإن قولك الرجل معناه الكامل

BURHAN:v4p324/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r10.speaker: النبي
BURHAN:v4p324/r10.claim: The Prophet’s saying كل الصيد في جوف الفرا illustrates that one who catches the falcon has, by its greatness, captured all game.
BURHAN:v4p324/r10.anchor: وإليه اشار بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم كل الصيد في جوف الفرا

BURHAN:v4p324/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p324/r11.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p324/r11.claim: Al-Ṣaffār allows this emphatic use only when the preceding word has an adjectival sense; it fails after a bare proper name such as عبد الله.
BURHAN:v4p324/r11.anchor: وهذا إنما يجوز إذا سبقها ما فيه رائحة الصفة كما ذكرنا فلو كان جامدا لم يجز

NAHHAS:v1p463/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p463/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p463/r12.claim: Alladhīna is the subject of inna, and sawfa nuṣlīhim nāran is its predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p463/r12.anchor: اسم إن والخبر ( سوف نصليهم نارا )

NAHHAS:v1p463/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p463/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p463/r13.anchor: ( كلما ) ظرف ( نضجت جلودهم ) بالإدغام لأن التاء من طرف اللسان

NAHHAS:v1p463/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p463/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p463/r14.claim: Assimilation of tāʾ into jīm is explained by their articulation points, but clear pronunciation is better to avoid a cluster of jīms.

NAHHAS:v1p463/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p463/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p463/r15.claim: God restores the cooked skin to an uncooked state, since the soul is what feels and knows; likewise the fire is rekindled whenever it dies down, as 17:97 says.
NAHHAS:v1p463/r15.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وقد ذكرنا في معناه قولين يرجعان إلى معنى واحد وهو أن المعنى إنا نعيد النضيج غير نضيج

NAHHAS:v1p463/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p463/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p463/r16.claim: The lām is purposive and makes the verb subjunctive, standing in place of an.
NAHHAS:v1p463/r16.anchor: منصوب بلام كي وهي بدل من أن

NAHHAS:v1p463/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p463/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p463/r17.claim: God is unconquerable and nothing escapes Him; He is wise in threatening His servants and in all His acts.
NAHHAS:v1p463/r17.anchor: أي لا يعجزه شيء ولا يفوته ( حكيما ) في إيعاده عباده وفي جميع أفعاله

ITQAN:v4p507/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p507/r2.speaker: معاذ
ITQAN:v4p507/r2.claim: In a weak Tabarani report, Muʿadh says the condemned skins are replaced one hundred times in an hour; ʿUmar says he heard this from the Prophet.
ITQAN:v4p507/r2.anchor: فقال معاذ عندي تفسيرها تبدل في ساعة مائة مرة فقال عمر هكذا سمعت من رسول الله

DAMGHANI:v1p63/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p63/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p63/r8.claim: Baddala can mean to renew or make anew; another example says the earth becomes a different creation.
DAMGHANI:v1p63/r8.anchor: الرابع : بدل بمعنى جدد . قوله تعالى في سورة النساء
